metric_definition: The organization’s ability to quickly adapt its strategic and operational supply chain response to demand and/or supply shocks. Strategic Supply Chain Agility is the number of days needed to meet a 25% unplanned change demand. Operational Supply Chain Agility is the sustained percentage increase or decrease in quantities that can be achieved in operational planning horizon (commonly 30 to 60 days).
metric_calculation: Strategic Supply Chain Agility is calculated by summing the planned lead times including source, transform, order, fulfill and plan. Operational Supply Chain Agility is calculated by dividing the new planned volume by the original planned volume. Both measures assume no expedite costs.

metric_definition: The organization’s ability to quickly adapt its strategic and operational order response to demand and/or supply shocks. Strategic Order Agility is the number of days needed to meet a 25% unplanned change in orders. Operational Order Agility is the sustained percentage increase or decrease in order quantities that can be achieved in operational planning horizon (commonly 30 to 60 days).
metric_calculation: Strategic Order Agility is calculated by identifying the master data setting for the assumed order lead times in your system of record. Operational Order Agility is calculated by dividing the new order volume by the original planned order volume. Both measures assume no expedite costs.

metric_definition: The organization’s ability to quickly adapt its strategic and operational source response to demand and/or supply shocks. Strategic Source Agility is the number of days needed to meet a 25% change in demand. Operational Source Agility is the sustained percentage increase or decrease in purchase order quantities that can be achieved in operational planning horizon (commonly 30 to 60 days).
metric_calculation: Strategic Source Agility is calculated by identifying the master data setting for the longest lead times in your BOM as noted in the system of record. Operational Source Agility is calculated by dividing the new increased or decreased purchase order volume by the original planned purchase order volume. Both measures assume no expedite costs.

metric_definition: The organization’s ability to quickly adapt its strategic and operational transform response to demand and/or supply shocks. Strategic Transform Agility is the number of days needed to meet a 25% unplanned change in demand. Operational Transform Agility is the sustained percentage increase in manufacturing and/or service orders that can be achieved in operational planning horizon (commonly 30 to 60 days).
metric_calculation: Strategic Transform Agility is calculated by identifying the master data setting for the manufacturing (service) lead time as noted in the system of record. Operational Transform Agility is calculated by dividing the new manufacturing and/or service order volume by the original planned order volume. Both measures assume no expedite costs.

metric_definition: The organization’s ability to quickly adapt its strategic and operational fulfill response to demand and/or supply shocks. Strategic Fulfill Agility is the number of days needed to meet a 25% unplanned change in demand. Operational Fulfill Agility is the sustained percentage increase or decrease in shipment quantities that can be achieved in operational planning horizon (commonly 30 to 60 days).
metric_calculation: Strategic Fulfill Agility is calculated by identifying the master data setting for the longest shipment lead times as noted in the system of record. Operational Fulfill Agility is calculated by dividing the new shipment volume by the original planned shipment volume. Both measures assume no expedite costs.

metric_definition: The organization’s ability to quickly adapt its strategic and operational return response to return requirement shocks. Strategic Return Agility is the number of days needed to meet a 25% unplanned change in returns. Operational Return Agility is the sustained percentage increase or decrease in return quantities that can be achieved in operational planning horizon (commonly 30 to 60 days).
metric_calculation: Strategic Return Agility is calculated by identifying the master data setting for the longest lead times in your returns process as noted in the system of record. Operational Return Agility is calculated by dividing the new return volume by the original planned return volume. Both measures assume no expedite costs.

metric_definition: Risk management in organizations traditionally resides within the finance function because of the subject’s inherent focus on financial impacts on the organization. However, many organizations do not assess supply chain risk separately. In recent years, supply chain risk management (SCRM) has become the focus area for finance executives responsible for enterprise risk management. Therefore, there is a need to establish a common language to quantify supply chain risk in terms of currency. Value at Risk (VaR) is a popular risk metric widely used by the finance industry to understand the risk exposure of a trading portfolio based on historic volatility.
Sum of time to place a purchase order and supplier lead time.
Current return volume in terms of number of orders returned.
Amount of each item purchased.

metric_name: Customer Return Order Cycle Time Reestablished And Sustained In 30 Days
metric_definition: Customer return order cycle time, including customer return order processing cycle time, transit time, return processing and disposition cycle time, reestablished and sustained for increased quantities returned from customer given 30 days.
Percentage of orders with on-time and accurate documentation supporting the order, including packing slips, bills of lading and invoices.

metric_name: Percentage Of Labor Used In Logistics But Not Used In Direct Activity
metric_definition: Percentage of labor used in logistics but not used in direct activity.

metric_name: Percentage Of Labor Used In Manufacturing But Not Used In Direct Activity
metric_definition: Percentage of labor used in manufacturing but not used in direct activity.
Additional customer return volume.
Additional delivery volume.

metric_name: Additional Source Volumes Obtained In 30 Days
metric_definition: Additional source volumes to be determined given ramped-up resources.
Current total number of items returned.
Number of orders shipped.
Amount of each item manufactured.

The time it takes for an investment made in raw materials to flow back into a company. For services, this represents the time from the point when a company pays for the resources consumed in the performance of a service to the time that the company receives payment from the customer for that service.
metric_calculation: Cash-to-Cash Cycle Time = Inventory Days of Supply + Days Sales Outstanding - Days Payable Outstanding

metric_definition: A measurement of the return an organization receives from its invested capital in supply chain fixed assets, including fixed assets used in Orchestrate, Plan, Order Source, Transfer, Fulfill and Return.
metric_calculation: Return on Supply Chain Fixed Assets = (Supply Chain Revenue – Total Supply Chain Management Cost (CO.1.1)) / Supply Chain Fixed Assets

metric_definition: A measurement that assesses the magnitude of investment relative to a company's working capital position versus the revenue generated from a supply chain. Components include accounts receivable, accounts payable, inventory, (Supply Chain) Revenue (AM.2.4), Total Supply Chain Management Cost (CO.1.1) and supply chain management costs.
metric_calculation: Return on Working Capital = (Supply Chain Revenue – Total Supply Chain Management Cost (CO.1.1)) / (Inventory + Accounts receivable – Accounts payable)

metric_definition: The length of time from when a sale is made until the payment for the sale is received from the customers. The amount of sales outstanding expressed in days.
metric_calculation: Five-point annual average of gross accounts receivable / (Total gross annual sales / 365 days)

metric_definition: The amount of inventory or stock expressed in days of sales. This metric also is known as days cost of sales in inventory and days sales in inventory, and it is the inverse of inventory turns.
metric_calculation:
Five-point rolling average of gross value of inventory at standard cost / Annual cost of goods sold] / 365 days

Example: If two items a day are sold and 20 items are held in inventory, this represents 10 days’ (20/2) worth of sales in inventory.

metric_definition: The length of time in days from purchasing materials, labor or conversion resources until cash payments must be made. This metric also is known as average payment period for materials, days purchases in accounts payable and days outstanding in accounts payable.
metric_calculation:
Five-point rolling average of gross accounts payable / Total gross annual material purchases / 365 days

The five-point rolling average calculation uses a combination of both historical and forward-looking data. This means that the rolling average value has to be calculated based on the average of both the four previous quarters and the projection for the current or next quarter. The five-point rolling average calculation is (Sum of the four previous quarters + Projection for the current or next quarter) / 5.

metric_definition: Operating revenue generated from a supply chain. This does not include non-operating revenue, such as leased real estate, investments, court settlements or sales of office buildings.
The sum of the fixed assets costs associated with Orchestrate, Plan, Order, Source, Transform, Fulfill, and Return fixed assets.
The amount of purchased materials, labor and conversion resources that need to be paid for. Also known as payables outstanding.
metric_calculation: The five-point rolling average of gross accounts payable.

metric_definition: The monetary value of accounts receivable outstanding expressed in dollars. Also known as sales outstanding.
metric_calculation: The five-point rolling average of gross accounts receivable

metric_definition: The monetary value of inventory or stock.
metric_calculation: (Sum of the four previous quarters + Projection for the current or next quarter) / 5

metric_name: Inventory Days Of Supply — Raw Material
metric_definition: Value of raw materials / (Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) (CO.1.2) / 365 days).

metric_name: Percentage Of Products Consisting Of Previously Used Components
metric_definition: The weight of recycled material in the product as a percentage of the total product weight.
Average age of excess inventory in days.

A measure of how intensively a resource is being used to produce a good or service. Some factors that should be considered are internal manufacturing capacity, constraining processes, direct labor availability, and key components and materials availability.
The average time associated with returns.

metric_name: Hazardous Materials Used During Production Process As A Percentage Of All Materials
metric_definition: The percentage by weight of material issued for production that is classified as hazardous material.

metric_name: Hazardous Waste As Percentage Of Total Waste
metric_definition: The percentage by weight of waste generated from production that is classified as hazardous material.

metric_name: Packaging As A Percentage Of Total Material
metric_definition: The percentage by weight of the total raw material that is classified as packaging material.
The number of returned products that are rebuilt or recycled as a percentage of the total number of products returned.

metric_name: Recyclable Waste As Percentage Of Total Waste
metric_definition: The percentage by weight of waste generated by production that is recyclable.
The number of returns that are for recycling or reuse as a percentage of the total number of products returned.

metric_name: Inventory Days Of Supply — Work In Process (Wip)
metric_definition: Total value of work in process / (Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) (CO.1.2) / 365 days).
The weight of products returned divided by the weight of products shipped.

metric_name: Percentage Of Defective Inventory In Disposition
metric_definition: The value of defective products awaiting a disposition decision as a percentage of the value of the total defective product inventory.
metric_calculation: Value of defective inventory in disposition stage / Total defective product inventory value x 100%.

metric_name: Percentage Of Defective Inventory In Return Authorization
metric_definition: The value of defective products awaiting return authorization as a percentage of the total defective product inventory value.
metric_calculation: Value of defective product inventory in request return authorization stage / Total defective product inventory value x 100%.

metric_name: Percentage Of Defective Product Inventory In Transportation
metric_definition: The value of defective product inventory in transportation as a percentage of the total defective product inventory.
metric_calculation: Value of defective product inventory in the physical return and transportation stage / Total defective product inventory value x 100%.

metric_name: Percentage Of Defective Product Inventory In Scheduling
metric_definition: The value of defective product inventory awaiting scheduling as a percentage of the total defective product inventory value.
metric_calculation: Value of defective product in scheduling stage / Total defective product inventory value x 100%

metric_name: Percentage Of Excess Inventory In Disposition
metric_definition: The value of excess inventory awaiting return in the disposition decision stage as a percentage of the total excess inventory value.
metric_calculation: Excess inventory in disposition stage / Total excess inventory value x 100%.

metric_name: Percentage Of Excess Inventory In Transportation
metric_definition: The value of excess product in the physical return and transportation stage as a percentage of the total excess product inventory value.
metric_calculation: Value of excess product in physical return and transportation stage / Total excess inventory value x 100%.

metric_name: Percentage Of Excess Inventory In Request Return Authorization
metric_definition: The value of excess inventory awaiting return authorization as a percentage of the total excess product inventory value.
metric_calculation: Value of excess product in request return authorization stage / Value of total excess inventory x 100%.

metric_name: Percentage Of Excess Inventory In Identification
metric_definition: The value of excess inventory awaiting return in the identification stage as a percentage of the total excess inventory value
metric_calculation: Value of excess inventory in identification stage / Total inventory value x 100%.

metric_name: Percentage Of Excess Inventory In Scheduling
metric_definition: The value of excess inventory awaiting scheduling as a percentage of the total excess inventory value. Calculation: Value of excess inventory in scheduling stage / Total inventory value x 100%.
The value of defective product inventory as a percentage of the value of total inventory.
metric_calculation: Total defective product inventory value / Total inventory value x 100%.

metric_name: Percentage Of Unserviceable Maintenance, Repair And Overhaul (Mro) Inventory In Disposition
metric_definition: The value of unserviceable MRO inventory in the disposition stage as a percentage of total MRO inventory value.
metric_calculation: Value of unserviceable MRO inventory in the disposition stage / Total MRO inventory value x 100%.

metric_name: Percentage Of Unserviceable Maintenance, Repair And Overhaul (Mro) Inventory In Transportation
metric_definition: The value of unserviceable MRO inventory in transportation as a percentage of the total MRO inventory value.
metric_calculation: Value of unserviceable MRO inventory in the transportation stage / Total MRO inventory value x 100%.

metric_name: Percentage Of Unserviceable Maintenance, Repair And Overhaul (Mro) Inventory In Return Authorization
metric_definition: The value of unserviceable MRO inventory awaiting return authorization as a percentage of the total MRO inventory value.
metric_calculation: Value of unserviceable MRO inventory in request return authorization stage / Total MRO inventory value x 100%.

metric_name: Percentage Of Unserviceable Maintenance, Repair And Overhaul (Mro) Inventory In Identification
metric_definition: The value of unserviceable MRO inventory awaiting identification as a percentage of the total MRO inventory value.
metric_calculation: Value of unserviceable MRO inventory in identification stage / Total MRO inventory value x 100%.

metric_name: Percentage Of Unserviceable Maintenance, Repair And Overhaul (Mro) Inventory In Scheduling
metric_definition: The value of unserviceable MRO inventory awaiting scheduling as a percentage of the total MRO inventory value.
metric_calculation: Value of unserviceable MRO inventory in scheduling stage / Total MRO inventory value x 100%.

metric_definition: The value of excess inventory as a percentage of the total inventory value.
metric_calculation: Value of excess inventory / Total inventory value x 100%.

metric_name: Inventory Days Of Supply — Finished Goods
metric_definition: Gross finished goods inventory / (Value of transfers / 365 days).

metric_name: Percentage Of The Product Content That Has A Supplier Take-Back Program For Recycling Or Reuse
metric_definition: Percentage of the product content, including packaging, that has a supplier take-back or recycling program. For example, some suppliers ship products in reusable containers or totes that can be returned, cleaned, and refilled.

metric_name: Percentage Of Materials That Are Recyclable Or Reusable
metric_definition: Percentage of the product content that is recyclable or reusable.

metric_name: Percentage Of Packaging And Shipping Materials Reused Internally
metric_definition: The percentage of scrap from packaging that is immediately reused in the packaging process.
The percentage of scrap from production that is immediately reused in the production process.

Total cost to manage order processing, acquire materials, manage inventory, and manage supply-chain finance, planning, and IT costs, as represented as a percent of revenue. Accurate assignment of IT-related cost is challenging. It can be done using Activity-Based-Costing methods or based on more traditional approaches. Allocation based on user counts, transaction counts, or departmental headcounts are reasonable approaches. The emphasis should be on capturing all costs, whether incurred in the entity completing the survey or incurred in a supporting organization on behalf of the entity. Reasonable estimates founded in data were accepted as a means to assess overall performance. All estimates reflected fully burdened actuals inclusive of salary, benefits, space and facilities, and general and administrative allocations.
metric_calculation:
Calculation: [Order Management Costs + Material Acquisition Costs + Inventory Carrying Costs + Supply-Chain-Related Finance and Planning Costs + Total Supply-Chain-Related IT Costs] / [Total Product Revenue]

(Please see individual component categories for component detail and calculations)

metric_definition:
The cost associated with buying raw materials and producing finished goods. This cost includes direct costs, such as labor and materials, and indirect costs, such as overhead.

Note: The cost of raw materials and production costs generally are accounted for in COGS. It is recognized that there likely is an overlap between supply chain management costs and COGS.
metric_calculation:
COGS = Cost to Transform

or

COGS = direct material costs + direct labor costs + indirect costs related to making a product

metric_definition: All costs associated with managing orders, including New Product Release Phase-In and Maintenance; Create Customer Order; Order Entry and Maintenance; Contract/Program and Channel Management; Installation Planning; Order Fulfillment; Distribution; Transportation, Outbound Freight and Duties; Installation; and Customer Invoicing/Accounting.

All costs associated with acquiring material, including Materials (Commodity) Management and Planning, Supplier Quality Engineering, Inbound Freight and Duties, Receiving and Material Storage, Incoming Inspection, Material Process and Component Engineering, and Tooling

All costs associated with carrying inventory, including Opportunity; Shrinkage; Insurance and Taxes; Total Obsolescence for Raw Material, WIP, and Finished Goods Inventory; Channel Obsolescence; and Field Service Parts Obsolescence.
All costs associated with supply chain finance and planning, including Supply-Chain Finance Costs and Demand/Supply Planning Costs.

Information Technology (IT) costs (in US dollars) associated with major supply-chain management processes as described below. These costs should include: Development costs (costs incurred in process reengineering, planning, software development, installation, implementation, and training associated with new and/or upgraded architecture, infrastructure, and systems to support the described supply-chain management processes), Execution costs (operating costs to support supply-chain process users, including computer and network operations, EDI and telecommunications services, and amortization/depreciation of hardware, Maintenance costs (costs incurred in problem resolution, troubleshooting, repair, and routine maintenance associated with installed hardware and software for described supply-chain management processes. Include costs associated with database administration, systems configuration control, release planning and management.
Direct cost spent on material for production.
Direct cost spent on labor for production.
Indirect cost incurred by or spent on production.

metric_name: New Product Release Phase-In And Maintenance
metric_definition: Costs associated with releasing new products to the field, maintaining released products, assigning product ID, defining configurations and packaging, publishing availability schedules, release letters and updates, and maintaining product databases.
Costs associated with creating invoice documents and processing (i.e., recording and capturing) customer payments.

All costs associated with supplier sourcing, contract negotiation and qualification, and the preparation, placement, and tracking of a purchase order. We recognize that these functions may be organizationally dispersed and/or decentralized but ask you to group all related costs for the purposes of this study. Also, this category includes all costs related to buyer/planners.
The costs associated with the determination, development/certification, and monitoring of suppliers' capabilities to fully satisfy the applicable quality and regulatory requirements.

Freight costs associated with the movement of material from a vendor to the buyer and the associated administrative tasks. Duties are those fees and taxes levied by government for moving purchased material across international borders. Customs brokers fees should also be considered in this category.
All costs associated with taking possession of material. This does not include inspection. Note that inventory-carrying costs are covered in a subsequent worksheet.
All costs associated with the inspection and testing of received materials to verify compliance with specifications.
Those tasks required to document and communicate component specifications, as well as reviews to improve the manufacturability of the purchased item.

Those costs associated with the design, development, and depreciation of the tooling required to produce a purchased item. A tooling cost would be incurred by a company if they actually paid for equipment and/or maintenance for a contract manufacturer that makes their product. Sometimes, there aren't enough incentive for a contract manufacturer to upgrade plant equipment to a level of quality that a company requires, so the company will pay for the upgrades and maintenance to ensure high quality. May not be common in some industries such as the Chemicals.

The opportunity cost of holding inventory. This should be based on your company's own cost of capital standards using the following formula. Calculation: Cost of Capital x Average Net Value of Inventory
The costs associated with breakage, pilferage, and deterioration of inventories. Usually pertains to the loss of material through handling damage, theft, or neglect.
Costs associated with creating and pricing configurations to order and preparing customer order documents.
The cost of insuring inventories and taxes associated with the holding of inventory.

metric_name: Total Obsolescence For Raw Material, Wip, And Finished Goods Inventory
metric_definition: Inventory reserves taken due to obsolescence and scrap and includes products exceeding the shelf life, i.e., spoils and is no good for use in its original purpose (do not include reserves taken for Field Service Parts).

Aging allowances paid to channel partners, provisions for buy-back agreements, etc. Includes all material that becomes obsolete while in a distribution channel. Usually, a distributor will demand a refund on material that goes bad (shelf life) or is no longer needed because of changing needs.

Reserves taken due to obsolescence and scrap. Field Service Parts are those inventories kept at locations outside the four walls of the manufacturing plant i.e., distribution center or warehouse. (This may be NA for some industries, e.g.: Chemicals)

Costs associated with paying invoices, auditing physical counts, performing inventory accounting, and collecting accounts receivable. Does NOT include customer invoicing/ accounting costs (see Order Management Costs).
Costs associated with forecasting, developing finished goods, intermediate, subassembly or end item inventory plans, and coordinating Demand/Supply
The percentage of Tariffs paid in the supply chain represented as a percentage of the company’s COGS.
Costs associated with maintaining the customer database, credit check, accepting new orders, and adding them to the order system as well as later order modifications.
Costs related to contract negotiation, monitoring progress, and reporting against the customer's contract, including administration of performance or warranty related issues.
Costs associated with installation engineering, scheduling and modification, handling cancellations, and planning the installation.
Costs associated with order processing, inventory allocation, ordering from internal or external suppliers, shipment scheduling, order status reporting, and shipment initiation.
Costs associated with warehouse space and management, finished goods receiving and stocking, processing shipments, picking, and consolidating, selecting carrier, and staging products/systems.
Costs associated with all company paid freight duties from point-of-manufacture to end-customer or channel.
Costs associated with verification of site preparation, installation, certification, and authorization of billing.
Total weight or volume of materials that are used to produce and package the organization’s primary products and service.
Total energy consumption within the organization, in joules or multiples.
metric_calculation: Total energy consumption within the organization = Non-renewable fuel consumed + Renewable fuel consumed + (Electricity, heating, cooling, and steam purchased for consumption) + Self-generated electricity, heating, cooling, and steam, which are not consumed - Electricity, heating, cooling, and steam sold

metric_definition: Total water consumption in megaliters.
metric_calculation: Total water consumption = Water Withdrawal - Water discharge

metric_definition: Metric tons of equivalent CO2 in Scope 1, 2 and 3, which includes all gases whether CO2, CH4, N2O, HFCs, PFCs, SF6, NF3, or other.
metric_calculation: GHG Emissions = Direct (Scope 1) GHG emissions + Energy indirect (Scope 2) GHG emissions + Other indirect (Scope 3) GHG emissions

metric_definition: Total weight of waste generated in metric tons.
Total weight or volume of renewable materials that are used to produce and package the organization’s primary products and services.
Percentage of waste diverted from disposal relative to the total weight of waste generated.
metric_calculation: Generated waste diverted from disposal = ((Waste diverted from disposal for reuse + Waste diverted from disposal for recycling + Waste diverted from disposal for other recovery options)/Waste generated) *100%

metric_definition: Percentage of waste directed to disposal relative to the total weight of waste generated.
metric_calculation: Generated waste directed to disposal = ((Waste directed to disposal for incineration / Waste generated) * 100%.

metric_definition: Total weight or volume of non-renewable materials that are used to produce and package the organization’s primary products and services.
Total renewable energy consumption within the organization, in joules or multiples.
Total nonrenewable energy consumption within the organization, in joules or multiples.
Total water withdrawal in megaliters.
Total water discharge in megaliters

Scope 1 emissions refer to emissions from owned or controlled boilers, furnaces, (air-conditioning) or vehicles and emissions from chemical production in owned or controlled process equipment. Methodologies used to calculate GHG emissions can include direct measurement of energy consumed, mass balance calculations, calculations based on site-specific data, calculations based on published criteria, direct measurement of GHG emissions and estimations. See GRI 305 for more information.

Scope 2 emissions refer to emissions from generated or purchased electricity, steam, heating, and cooling consumed by the company. Scope 2 emissions physically occur at the facility where the electricity, steam, heating, and cooling is generated. Methodologies used to calculate Energy indirect (Scope 2) GHG emissions: location-based value and market-based value. See GRI 305 for more information.
Scope 3 emissions are emissions as a consequence of the activities of the company that occur from sources not owned or controlled by the company.

metric_name: Reclaimed Products And Their Packaging Materials
metric_definition: The percent of reclaimed input materials used to manufacture the organization’s primary products and services.

metric_definition: Percentage of the product content that is recyclable or reusable.
Percentage of materials that is actually recycled or reused.
Percentage of Circularity = Weighted average of Percentage of Circular inflow and Percentage of Circular outflow.
The energy required per unit of activity, output, or any other organization-specific metric.
The water withdrawal required per unit of activity, output, or any other organization-specific metric.
The amount of GHG emissions per unit of activity, output, or any other organization-specific metric.
Number of successful troubleshooting and returns avoided over total number of customer outreaches.

Conformance to country or union law. Example: responsible disposal laws in the EU

metric_name: Disposition Mix Compared To Target Mix

Amount of GHG avoided due to renewal of product/services and associated warehouse/transportation/logistics improvement

metric_definition: integration standardization throughout end-to-end supply chains allows different systems to hook up in a plug and play manner instead of initial development and continual updates based on individual user activities

metric_definition: Cost of Restoration of Future Economic Benefit by product family includes cost to renew, scrap, or salvage per time period. Activity by entity to restore up to 100% of original value of units/offering.
Percentage of materials that is virgin materials, not recycled or reused before this use.
Total renewable energy sold, in joules or multiples
Total nonrenewable energy sold, in joules or multiples
The rate of water reuse and recycling is a measure of efficiency and demonstrates success in reducing total water withdrawals and discharges.

metric_name: Waste Diverted From Disposal For Reuse
metric_definition: Percentage of waste diverted from disposal for reuse relative to the total weight of waste generated.
metric_calculation: (waste diverted from disposal for reuse/total weight of waste generated) *100

metric_definition: Percentage of waste diverted from disposal for recycling relative to the total weight of waste generated.
metric_calculation: (waste diverted from disposal for recycling/total weight of waste generated) *100

metric_definition: Percentage of waste diverted from disposal for other recovery options relative to the total weight of waste generated.

metric_name: Earnings Before Interest And Taxes (Ebit) As A Percent Of Revenue
metric_definition: A measure of a company's earning power from ongoing operations, equal to earnings (revenues minus cost of sales, operating expenses, and taxes) before deduction of interest payments and income taxes, also called operating profit. EBIT = Revenue - COGS - Operating Expenses
metric_calculation: EBIT = Revenue - COGS - Operating Expenses.

metric_definition: The effective tax rate is the average tax rate paid by a corporation or an individual. Tax-efficient supply chains can significantly impact this rate.

The percentage of orders meeting delivery performance expectations, including complete and accurate documentation and no delivery damage. According to the APICS Dictionary, a perfect order satisfies the seven R’s: the right product and/or service, the right quantity, the right condition, the right place, the right time (which should be measured by the customer’s definition of on time), the right customer and the right cost. Perfect Order Fulfillment addresses all of these and considers the presence of all proper documentation, including packing slips, bills of lading, invoices and more.

Right product and/or service and right quantity are grouped into the level-2 metric Percentage of Orders Delivered in Full to the Customer (RL.2.1). Right time, right location and right customer are grouped into the level-2 metric Delivery Performance to Original Customer Commit Date (RL.2.2). Right condition is measured by the level-2 metric Customer Order Perfect Condition (RL.2.4). Right cost is measured by the overall Cost strategic attribute. Lastly, proper documentation is measured by Customer Order Documentation Accuracy (RL.2.3).
metric_calculation:
(Total perfect orders / Total number of orders) x 100%

Note: An order is perfect if the individual line items making up that order are all perfect.

The Perfect Order Fulfillment calculation is based on the performance of each level-2 component of the order line to be calculated (product and quantity; date, time and customer; documentation; and condition). For an order line to be perfect, all of the individual components must be perfect:

An order is considered perfect if the products ordered are the products provided and the quantities ordered match the quantities provided. (See Percentage of Orders Delivered In Full to the Customer (RL.2.1).)
A delivery is considered perfect if the product or service is given to the right customer at the right place and at the right time. (See Delivery Performance to Original Customer Commit Date (RL.2.2).)
Documentation supporting the order line is considered perfect if it is all accurate, complete and on time. (See Customer Order Accurate Documentation (RL.2.3).)
The product condition is considered perfect if the product is not damaged, meets customer specifications, is in the right configuration, is faultlessly installed (if applicable) and is accepted by the customer. (See Customer Order Perfect Condition (RL.2.4).) Each component receives a score of 1 if it is judged to be perfect. Otherwise, it receives a score of zero. If the sum of the scores equals the number of components (in this case, four), the order line is perfectly fulfilled.

metric_definition: The percentage of orders from the supplier meeting delivery performance expectations, including complete and accurate documentation and no delivery damage. According to the APICS Dictionary, a perfect order satisfies the seven R’s: the right product, the right quantity, the right condition, the right place, the right time (which should be measured by the customer’s definition of on time), the right customer and the right cost. Perfect Supplier Order Fulfillment addresses all of these and considers the presence of all proper documentation, including packing slips, bills of lading, invoices and more. Right product and right quantity are grouped into the level-2 metric Percentage of Orders Delivered In Full from the Supplier (RL.2.5). Right time, right location, and right customer are grouped into the level-2 metric Delivery Performance to Original Supplier Commit Date (RL.2.6), Right condition is measured by the level-2 metric Supplier Order Perfect Condition (RL.2.8). Right cost is measured by the overall Cost strategic attribute. Lastly, proper documentation is measured by Supplier Order Documentation Accuracy (RL.2.7).

The percentage of orders delivery performance expectations, including complete and accurate documentation and no delivery damage. According to the APICS Dictionary, a perfect order satisfies the seven R’s: the right product, the right quantity, the right condition, the right place, the right time (which should be measured by the customer’s definition of on time), the right customer and the right cost. Perfect Return Order Fulfillment addresses all of these and considers the presence of all proper documentation, including packing slips, bills of lading, invoices and more. Right product and right quantity are grouped into the level-2 metric "On Time (RL.2.9)". Right time, right location and right customer are grouped into the level-2 metric Delivery Performance to "In Full (Correct Product) (RL.2.10)". Right condition is measured by the level-2 metric "Perfect Condition (RL.2.12)". Right cost is measured by the overall Cost strategic attribute. Lastly, proper documentation is measured by "Correct Documentation (RL.2.11)".
